claim: Ambedkar defined constitutional morality as a sentiment that is not natural but must be cultivated, noting that his people had yet to learn it.
He argued that without this cultivated morality, democracy remains fragile, and extra-constitutional methods like satyagraha must be ruled out in post-independent politics.
Ambedkar argued that caste denies democratic ideals by organizing society on rigid lines that prevent Indians from eating, marrying, or voting freely.
He believed the Brahmin caste would oppose abolition because it would destroy their own power and prestige within Hindu society.
संवैधानिक नैतिकता का अर्थ है संविधान के नियमों का गहरा सम्मान, जिसमें सत्ता के प्रति अनुपालन और उस पर निष्पक्ष आलोचना का मिश्रण शामिल है।
यह एक प्राकृतिक भावना नहीं है, बल्कि इसे संस्कृति करना होगा, क्योंकि भारतीय समाज अभी इसे सीखने में असमर्थ है।
